HUNTING STUDIES, 2026-11-13
Three ways to act on a big move, measured on 45 sessions of the whole US market. Costs taken off. Doing nothing scores 0%.

1. FLAG STUDY
A jump of 20%+ on at least 5x normal volume, then 3+ quiet days on drying volume, then a break above the quiet range. Bought on the break, stop at the bottom of the range, out after 5 sessions.

CONCLUSION: Too few finished flag trades in these 45 sessions to judge. It needs more weeks.

What became of 252 heavy-volume jumps: 221 never formed a flag, 11 formed one and broke down, 7 went nowhere, 1 gapped away with no fair entry, 12 broke out and gave an entry.
All flag trades: average -3.0%, typical -1.0%, 18% ended higher (11 trades)
5 USD and over: average -1.4%, typical -0.9%, 22% ended higher (9 trades)
Under 5 USD: average -10.3%, typical -4.7%, 0% ended higher (2 trades)
Compare, buying the morning after the jump: typical -3.8%, 40% ended higher (837 cases).

2. FLAG PULLBACK (after the break, wait for a return to the break level that holds)
5 USD and over: average -4.1%, typical -0.9%, 29% ended higher (7 trades)

3. EXPANSION DAY (up 1.5x its normal daily range or more on 2x volume or more; bought at the next open; stop 1x that range, target 3x, out after 10 sessions)
5 USD and over: average +0.3%, typical -1.7%, 36% ended higher (466 trades). Of these, 29% reached the target, 62% hit the stop, 9% ran out of time.
Under 5 USD: average -3.6%, typical -6.1%, 16% ended higher (63 trades)
CONCLUSION: the expansion day made a little on average but lost more often than it won. Not usable as it stands.
A target three times the stop is reached far less often than the stop. The numbers above are what that trade-off really paid.
